title: Iran Threatens 'Heavy Assault' as Tanker War Escalates
excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guard warns US bases are targets after American jets disable two Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman.
body:
Iran's Revolutionary Guard issued its most direct military threat in weeks on Saturday, May 10, warning that any further attacks on Iranian vessels would trigger a 'heavy assault' on US bases and warships across the Middle East — even as a fragile ceasefire technically remains in place.

**What Happened:**
Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy warned that any attack on Iranian oil tankers or commercial vessels would be met with a 'heavy assault' on one of the US bases in the region and enemy ships. Iranian state TV reported the warning a day after the United States struck two Iranian oil tankers, casting doubt on the month-old ceasefire that the US has insisted is still in effect. US Central Command said the military had disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers as they attempted to access Iranian ports in the Gulf of Oman.

**Why This Moment Matters:**
Washington is awaiting an Iranian response to its latest proposal for a deal to end the war, reopen the strait, and roll back Tehran's disputed nuclear program. Talks between the US and Iran are being mediated by Pakistan, with issues under discussion including freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear and ballistic program, reconstruction, sanctions, and a long-term peace agreement. The Iranian effort to formalize control over the channel raised new concerns about international shipping, with hundreds of commercial vessels bottled up in the Persian Gulf and unable to reach the open sea.

**What to Watch:**
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said his country has been in contact with the US and Iran 'day and night' in an effort to extend the ceasefire and reach a peace deal. The ceasefire has been extended, but there is no sign of further talks on a broad deal.
